To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Community energy projects in Wales are more likely to be supported by local authorities, and have greater opportunities for funding, than their counterparts in Scotland, which in turn are likely to be more supported by the Scottish Government.
the devolved nations in Scotland and Wales have different approaches to community energy and that these approaches are shaped by different political and institutional contexts.

the devolved nations' policy and governance practices influence community energy practitioners' confidence in the sector, and their perceptions of the sector's potential to contribute towards a low-carbon economy and a more sustainable, localised economic model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the sector has been influenced by policy and governance, and the implications this has for community energy practitioners in Wales and Scotland.
how community energy projects can be supported to flourish in Scotland and Wales.
how community energy practitioners experience planning and policy in their efforts to develop community-owned renewable energy projects.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
community energy projects in the devolved nation of Wales are more likely to be successful and sustainable than in Scotland.
the community energy sector in Scotland is currently in a more favourable and stable position than in Wales.
the sector has the potential to grow, and that there are a variety of ways in which it can be supported.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is a need for policy and planning to support the sector, as well as a need for a greater understanding of the barriers and enablers of community energy projects in the UK, and beyond.
the sector is not yet fully supported in Wales, whereas it has a more secure future in Scotland.
community energy is not a panacea, but it is a valuable tool in a climate change mitigation toolkit.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the sector is not homogenous, but is instead a diverse and complex field, which is shaped by local, national, and international contexts and actors.
community energy projects in Scotland and Wales are not experiencing the same level of support from policy and governance structures.
the sector is in need of a supportive governance environment, which can facilitate its expansion.
